what_this_is: The Workshop rows that reach the person's own signed-in browser from a tool run on their computer: reading a page, acting on one and driving a session. Each runs ask-my-browser.mjs, which posts to the browser relay door the extension's native messaging host opens on this computer (browser-relay.mjs).

payload.label: Read a page in my browser
payload.job: Open a page in the person's own browser, signed in as they are, and read what it shows
payload.description: Opens the page at url in a window of its own that is not brought forward, in the browser the person is signed in to, waits for it to load, reads it and closes the window. Answers { url, title, text, links } as the loaded page shows them, so a page that needs the person's sign-in or refuses requests from servers can still be read. Refused in words when no browser is connected to this computer.

verify.requires: a computer whose report names the port `browser-relay` (its `local_ports`), and a browser the person is signed in to with the browser extension that holds this computer's connection allowed to talk to it; with no browser connected every run is refused in words, so no sample can exit 0; and the Ed25519 key `browser-relay-key` made in the person's vault (the workflow make-a-signing-key-in-the-vault)

provenance.source: a browser extension's page-reading code, whose runs reached the browser over an account route that is retired; now relayed through the person's own computer (browser-relay.mjs)

payload.label: Act on a page in my browser
payload.job: Click, type, press keys, scroll and choose on a page in the person's own browser, signed in as they are, and read the page again after
payload.description: Opens the page at url in a window of its own that is not brought forward, validates steps (page-actions.json), does them in order, reads the page again and answers what each step did with the page after. dry_run only locates every target and acts on none. Refused in words when no browser is connected to this computer.

steps.description: The steps to do: a list of { do, target, ... }

dry_run.description: true locates every target and does nothing

verify.requires: a computer whose report names the port `browser-relay` (its `local_ports`), and a browser the person is signed in to with the browser extension that holds this computer's connection allowed to talk to it; with no browser connected every run is refused in words, so no sample can exit 0; and the Ed25519 key `browser-relay-key` made in the person's vault (the workflow make-a-signing-key-in-the-vault)

provenance.source: a browser extension's page-reading code, whose runs reached the browser over an account route that is retired; now relayed through the person's own computer (browser-relay.mjs)

payload.label: Drive my browser
payload.job: Drive a web page across several calls through the person's own signed-in browser, in a window of its own, until they take it back
payload.description: One call of a browser session (browser-session.json): do is tabs, open, close, navigate, back, forward, act, read, lock, release or end, with the session, tab, url and steps that verb needs. The session owns an unfocused window and only the tabs it opened; the person's own tabs are never touched; the person's lock takes the browser back at once. Refused in words when no browser is connected to this computer.

do.description: tabs, open, close, navigate, back, forward, act, read, lock, release or end

verify.requires: a computer whose report names the port `browser-relay` (its `local_ports`), and a browser the person is signed in to with the browser extension that holds this computer's connection allowed to talk to it; with no browser connected every run is refused in words, so no sample can exit 0; and the Ed25519 key `browser-relay-key` made in the person's vault (the workflow make-a-signing-key-in-the-vault)

payload.label: Read a page in a scriptable browser
payload.job: Open a page in the person's own scriptable browser app, signed in as they are, read what it shows and close the tab, when no browser extension is connected to this computer
payload.description: Opens the page at url as a new tab in the browser app named by computer["automate-an-app"].app (its bundle id; Arc is company.thebrowser.Browser), waits for it to load, reads its title, visible text, links and image urls with one fixed read-only script, and closes the tab. It never types, clicks, submits or sets anything on the page, and never starts the app: a browser that is not open is refused in words. If the Mac has not allowed this to control the browser, it answers needs_access "automation" with what to allow.

computer.description: The computer's capability: { "automate-an-app": { "app": "<bundle id of the browser>" } }

verify.requires: a computer whose browser app (bundle id named in computer["automate-an-app"].app) is open and allowed to be controlled by the Mac app that runs the tool (System Settings, Privacy & Security, Automation); proved by reading a public page and the bookmarks page read-only

provenance.source: Made 2026-11-21 as the second route for reading a page when no browser extension is connected: the Chromium-style AppleScript dictionary of a scriptable browser (tab URL, loading, execute javascript, close) driven through osascript, the way tool:send-a-message-on-this-mac drives Messages with automate-an-app
